chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibrahim al-Kazzaz from Abd al-Hamid ibn Awadd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"If you are leading a congregation, one greeting to your right suffices for you; and if you are with an Imam, two greetings; and if you are alone, one greeting facing the Qibla."

key_terms.تَسْلِيمَةٌ: A greeting of peace (salam) concluding the prayer

ai.seo_question: How many salams should one make in prayer when leading, following, or praying alone?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural nuances of concluding the prayer (taslim) based on the worshipper's role, distinguishing between leading a congregation, following an Imam, or praying individually. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precision in ritual acts, noting that a single salam suffices for the leader while two are required for the follower to ensure synchronization with the Imam's conclusion. This ruling underscores the communal harmony and structural integrity of congregational prayer as derived from the Ahl al-Bayt.
